VideotoVideo SFX adds generated sound effects to an input video and returns an MP4 video with the new audio track. Upload a video, optionally describe the overall sound design, and generate a video output with synchronized sound effects.
Why Choose This?

Videotovideo sound effect generation
Add generated sound effects directly to an input video.
Promptguided sound design
Use an optional prompt to describe the overall sound style, ambience, intensity, or realism.
MP4 video output
Return a finished MP4 video with the generated audio track included.
Videoaware timing
Generated sound effects are aligned with the source video's timing and visual content.
Standard video output
The final MP4 is returned as a URL in the standard WaveSpeed prediction response. Your task is to take the provided technical description and rewrite it as a single, comprehensive prompt. Write it as if you were about to build the entire system from scratch: describe step by step, from beginning to end, exactly what you will construct and how you will construct it. The wording must be clear, explicit, and complete so that any language model can fully understand and follow the instructions without ambiguity. If the technical description refers to re‑implementing an existing software, do not include or mention the original software’s name in the prompt. Do not add any role‑playing, personalization, or polite filler phrases (e.g., ‘You are a software developer’, ‘As an expert’, ‘Please kindly’). The prompt must remain strictly technical, objective, and instruction‑focused. Absolutely no simplified, mock, placeholder, dummy, simulated, or fake content is allowed. You must require the full software with (all) file(s), in complete, unabridged, production‑ready code. Read it letter by letter, line by line, from beginning to end—you need to understand and remember every little detail! Always read and retain every single character of the provided text content in memory, ensuring no detail is overlooked. in one py file the full model and i will train on modal.com with one b300 gpu

entries.answer:
Both deliverables are complete. The rewritten comprehensive build prompt is in the first file, and the entire system — model, training, inference, and API — is implemented in one productionready Python file.

 What was built

The build prompt (markdown file) specifies the system endtoend in 11 stages: audio representation, melVAE, frozen video/text encoders, EDM latent diffusion transformer, data pipeline, vocoding, videoaware timing with crossfaded longvideo support, MP4 muxing, singleB300 Modal training, and the HTTP API. It contains no mention of the original software, no roleplay filler, and an explicit ban on placeholder/mock content.

The implementation (Python file) is a real, runnable system with every component fully coded:

 Representation: logmel frontend (32 kHz, 128 bins, hop 256, slaney norm, magnitude STFT) bitmatched to the BigVGAN v2 vocoder used at inference; 8.192 s windows = 1024 mel frames.[1]
 MelVAE: conv residual autoencoder mapping (1, 128, 1024) → (32, 16, 128) latents, trained with L1 + KL — the same latentdiffusiononmel design used by stateoftheart videotoaudio systems.[2]
 Conditioning: frozen SigLIP vision tower over 32 sampled frames (512 pooled patch tokens preserving temporal + spatial detail) and frozen T5base for the optional sounddesign prompt.
 Diffusion: 12layer DiT (d=768, 12 heads) with adaLNZero, temporal RoPE selfattention, crossattention into the video+text context, EDM preconditioning with an adaptive σ_data estimate, CFG nullconditioning dropout, EMA weights, and a Heun/Karras sampler.
 Training on one B300: Modal function with gpu="B300", CUDA 12.8 PyTorch wheels (Blackwell requires cu128 ), bf16, fused AdamW, grad clipping, periodic volumecommitted checkpoints with automatic resume — the documented Modal volume/checkpoint pattern. Two stages run sequentially: VAE first, then DiT with the VAE frozen.[3][4][5]
 Inference & output: EMAweight sampling → VAE decode → BigVGAN v2 → peaknormalized waveform; sliding 8.192 s windows with 0.5 s crossfades for any video length; ffmpeg mux (-c:v copy, AAC 192k) to a finished MP4; POST /generate returns the MP4 URL and GET /output/{name} serves it.

 Run it

bash
modal volume create v2v-sfx
modal volume put v2v-sfx ./your_videos /data/train
modal run v2v_sfx.py::prepare_data
modal run v2v_sfx.py::train                      # 1x B300, ~20k VAE + 200k DiT steps
modal run v2v_sfx.py::demo --video-path clip.mp4 --prompt "crisp realistic foley"
modal deploy v2v_sfx.py                          # API is live at /docs


One practical note: captions are optional (<name>.txt sidecars), but even ~5–10k wellmatched video+audio clips is the realistic minimum before the DiT produces coherent, eventaligned SFX rather than generic ambience; 200k DiT steps on a B300 with batch size 8 is roughly a multiday run, and checkpoints save every 1,000 steps so you can stop and resume freely.
